messages.body_plain:
Using the scale_color_manual() you can manually set the colors. There is also a scale_linetype_manual if you want, but I didn't bother to include it.

library(ape)
library(ggtree)

tree1 <- rtree(5)
tree2 <- rtree(5)

#make three groups we will make "a" blue, "b" green, and "c" red"
tree1_tax <- list(a=c("t1"), b=c("t2", "t3"), c=c("t4","t5"))
#now we condense "b" and "c", which will become red
tree2_tax <- list(a=c("t1"), b=c("t2", "t3", "t4", "t5"))

#now make the groups
tree1_groups <- groupOTU(tree1, tree1_tax)
tree2_groups <- groupOTU(tree2, tree2_tax)

#using the scale_color_manual, we can setup the color groups manually
tree1_test <- ggtree(tree1_groups, aes(color=group)) + scale_color_manual(values=c("blue", "green","red")) + theme(legend.position="right") + geom_tiplab()
tree2_test <- ggtree(tree2_groups, aes(color=group)) + scale_color_manual(values=c("blue","red"))               + theme(legend.position="right") + geom_tiplab()

plot(tree1_test)
plot(tree2_test)

messages.body_plain:
Hi Guy,

Rooting these objects is something that needs to be done very thoughtfully. See http://www.biorxiv.org/content/early/2017/01/13/035360 for what can go wrong if rerooting is done improperly. You didn't attach any code, so not sure if you are using ggtree::reroot or the new version of ape::root, but don't use ggtree::reroot if you want to keep node-associated values. Personally if I want to change the rooting, I just get the phylogenetics program to re-output with the topology I want displayed.

Assuming you are using the newest version of ape::root, then see https://rdrr.io/cran/ape/man/root.html. In the examples section they walk through how if you want to avoid the basal trichomy you need to root using the outgroup, not by designating the node (which they designate using 1:5 in the birdorders example).

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am also trying to assign different sets of colors to different panels. Currently, if you apply a set of colors to the first panel and a second set of colors to the second panel the new scale will replace the existing one if the number of levels is the same between the two dataframes or give and error if the the number of levels is  different.

E.g.

p<-ggtree(tr)

#adding a panel with a bar chart using a 3 levels variable to fill colors

p1<-facet_plot(p, panel="Panel1", data=data1, geom=geom_barh, mapping=aes(x=value, fill= as.factor(groups)), stat='identity') + scale_fill_manual(values=c("#359946", "#EA2227", "#C8D92D"))

#adding a second panel with a different bar chart using a 2 levels variable to fill colors

p2<-facet_plot(p1, panel="Panel2", data=data2, geom=geom_barh, mapping=aes(x=value, fill= as.factor(groups2)), stat='identity') + scale_fill_manual(values=c("blue", "red"))

In this case you will receive as error:

"Insufficient values in manual scale, 5 needed but only 2 provided". This is because is summing up the levels from the two different panels. If you use a color scale for the first panel and a fill scale for the second you can partially fix it but the result is not 100% the desired result. Is there a way to fix this behavior?

Thanks!

Brigida

gg <- ggtree(tree)
for (i in 1:3){
  gg <- gg+geom_hilight(nds[i],cls[i],alpha = alphas[i])

gg
